newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China "pot of gold" for duty free sales -executive.
newsitem.headline: China "pot of gold" for duty free sales -executive.

text.p: The international tax free shopping market in China promises a pot of gold for retailers and Hong Kong will be crucial to companies aiming to tap into it, an industry leader predicted on Tuesday.

"(Hong Kong's new) Chek Lap Kok (airport) will be the gateway to the Middle Kingdom and will set the standards for Airport Duty Free in China," said Antares Cheng, managing director of the King Power Group.
The International Air Transport Association predicts a further doubling of passenger traffic by 2000 and this could bring a commensurate boost to duty free sales, he said.

Add in the roughly 200 million passengers travelling by land and sea in 1996 -- and it was clear to see China offered "a sumptuous menu of opportunities" and held "the greatest future potential for the duty free industry", Cheng said.
"Hong Kong will be the key model and catalyst for the economic development and the creation of wealth in the China of tomorrow," Cheng told the annual Tax Free Asia Pacific trade fair in Singapore.
"Let us assure you there is a "pot of gold"," he said.

Cheng said visitor arrivals in China had leapt from 26.9 million in 1987 to 51.1 million in 1996 and duty free sales at just two Chinese airports -- Beijing and Shanghai Honggiao -- already top US$30 million every year.
